# dsh-browser
Give your DeepSeek Harness agent a real browser — and watch it work.

A live Chromium for every DSH session: the agent drives it, you watch it in a
panel inside the UI, a

nd you can take over with your own mouse and keyboard at
any time. Backed by a ranked search gateway

(SearXNG, Google CSE, Gemini, Brave,
Vertex, DuckDuckGo) with whole-web Google results.
## How it fits together
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What you get

- **Live panel** — every page the agent opens, as it happens; take over
instantly (your clicks and k

eys go to the same tab). Resizable card, tabs
strip, address bar, maximize mode.
- **Ranked search**

— whole-web Google results via Gemini grounding; Brave,
SearXNG, Vertex, DuckDuckGo reorderable; fi

rst provider that answers wins,
the rest are fallback. Keys live in one settings page, never shown a

gain.
- **One session, one browser** — the browser session id *is* the DSH session
id, created on fi

rst use; isolated profile, cookies and tabs per session;
idle sessions close themselves, and deletin

g a workspace closes the browser
sessions attached to it.

17 agent tools: navigate, snapshot, click, type, press, scroll, tabs,
screenshot, search, wait_for,

find, batch, console, network. CAPTCHA or
consent page? The agent pauses and asks — you finish it in

the panel, by
design, never automated.
## Try it
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Only the gateway port (8787) is published. The browser, viewer, SearXNG, and
Brave MCP stay on the c

ompose network. For a remote DSH host, bind the gateway
to a private/VPN address (or use an SSH tunn

el) and enter its URL in the plugin
page.
### Configuration
| Where | Setting | Default | Notes |
| Stack `.env` | `GATEWAY_BIND` | `127.0.0.1` | Host interface for the only published backend port.

Use a private/VPN IP for a remote DSH; `0.0.0.0` only behind a firewall. |
| Stack `.env` | `GATEWAY

_PORT` | `8787` | Host gateway port. |
| Stack `.env` | search/browser settings | see `.env.example`

| Optional stack/host-dev knobs. Search keys can be set in the plugin UI. |
| DSH UI | **Stack gate
way address** | `http://127.0.0.1:8787` | One URL only; persisted. Use the local URL when the backen

d is on this host, otherwise the backend’s reachable URL. |
| DSH env (optional) | `DSH_BROWSER_GATE
WAY_URL` | unset | First-run seed only. Normal setups use the UI. |

For Cloudflare Tunnel or a reverse proxy, keep `GATEWAY_BIND=127.0.0.1` and
point the tunnel at `htt

p://127.0.0.1:8787`. The public HTTPS URL goes in the
plugin UI; no stack port needs to be exposed.
Install the panel plugin (UI or CLI)
**From the DSH UI** — open the `?token=` URL DSH printed:

1. **Plugins** in the sidebar
2. **Add plugin**
3. paste `github:codeadeel/dsh-browser#path:panel` i

nto the **package field**
(leave **Registry** on the default npm registry — its custom address is fo

The panel registers the ranked search tool natively. There is no separate
MCP client, DSH patch, or
`--patch` flag to add.
**From the CLI:**
[代码示例省略，未执行]

For a local dev link, run `pnpm install` in the repo first so the panel's
`ws` dependency resolves.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Click the **Browser** button. In **Plugins → dsh-browser-panel** set the
**Stack gateway address** (

default `http://127.0.0.1:8787`; a remote stack
uses its public/private gateway URL), choose your pr

ovider order, save, and
run **Test search**.

Then ask the agent: *"search for the DeepSeek R2 release date, open the top
result, and summarize it
"* — and watch it happen in the panel.
## How a search works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- Gemini = whole-web Google grounding, AI Studio key, billing required. Move Gemini above earlier pr

oviders to force it; the first provider that answers wins.
- Brave = a UI key uses Brave REST immedi

ately. The optional brave-mcp service uses `BRAVE_API_KEY` from the stack `.env` at startup.
- SearX

NG = free, self-hosted, no key. Vertex = site-scoped app search.
- One gateway address for everythin

g, set in the plugin page: search at the
root, browser at `/browser`, viewer at `/viewer`. `DSH_BROW

SER_GATEWAY_URL`
is only a first-run seed. The stack can live on another machine. Plain HTTP
end to
end unless you put it behind TLS.
## How the browser works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why it exists

- **Trust through visibility** — you see exactly what the agent is doing, no
more blind tool calls.

- **Human in the loop, not in the way** — same browser for both drivers, no
VNC, no extension, no sc

reen-recording hacks.
- **Search that keeps up** — Gemini grounding gives current whole-web results;

SearXNG and Brave cover privacy and cost.
- **No private registry, zero accounts** — first-party se

rvices build from
source; SearXNG runs from its official image.
